title: Finite point internal-Hom evaluation comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For every $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A_n)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], put $c=\operatorname{Fib}_s(C)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and $\omega_{s,n}=Ra_s^!(A_n)_s$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The canonical evaluation-transpose map, formed using the point-fibre tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] and the derived sheaf internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-pur-derived-internal-hom],
$$
\kappa_C:\operatorname{Fib}_s igl(R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(C,\omega_{s,n}) igr)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(c,A_n),
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $C$. The normalization $\omega_{s,n}\cong(A_n)_s$ is the following one: for $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$ with the identity compactification the etale compact support is the identity and its right adjoint is $a_s^	imes=\operatorname{id}$, so $\omega_{s,n}=
u_s^*R
u_{s,*}(A_n)_s$ for the comparison morphism $
u_s:s_{\mathrm{proet}}	o s_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and the normalization is the counit $
u_s^*R
u_{s,*}(A_n)_s	o(A_n)_s$, which is an isomorphism because $(A_n)_s=
u_s^*(A_n)_s$ and the unit $\operatorname{id}	o R
u_{s,*}
u_s^*$ is an isomorphism on bounded-below etale complexes [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. The map $\kappa_C$ is characterized by evaluation: after identifying $\omega_{s,n}\cong(A_n)_s$, the coefficient evaluation composed with $\kappa_C\otimes 1_c$ is the point-fibre of the sheaf evaluation.

source.place: Opening paragraph: at the identity point, the dualizing object is the coefficient unit and the displayed identification of D_s is the coefficient-module dual, computed by the derived internal Hom definition.

proof.text:
Write $A=A_n$, $B=A_s$, $G=A_{s,\mathrm{et}}$ and $
u=
u_s$. The absolute value of $E$ extending $|\cdot|_\ell$ is nonarchimedean by the extension-absolute-value theorem, and the valuation-ring theorem makes $R$ a DVR with finite residue field; the finite-quotient theorem, clause (2), then makes $A=R/\varpi^n$ a finite ring. For the identity compactification on the etale point, $R\operatorname{id}_!^{\mathrm{et}}=R\operatorname{id}_*\operatorname{id}_!=\operatorname{id}$ by the compact-support definition. Its right adjoint is canonically the identity: its adjunction bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}(U,V)=\operatorname{Hom}(U,V)$. The finite exceptional-inverse-image definition therefore gives $\omega_{s,n}=
u^*R
u_*B$. The constant-ring comparison identifies $B=
u^*G$. Let $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ be the unit and counit of $
u^*\dashv R
u_*$. The bounded-below site-comparison theorem makes $\eta_G$ invertible, since $G$ is in degree zero. The triangle identity $\epsilon_{
u^*G}\circ
u^*(\eta_G)=1_{
u^*G}$ now shows that $\epsilon_B$ is the inverse of $
u^*(\eta_G)$. Thus the normalization $\alpha:\omega_{s,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ is precisely the counit required in the statement, not an arbitrary unit identification.

source.place: Opening sentence: identity compact support and its right adjoint; finite transported normalization made explicit.

proof.text: Put $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline M=\underline M$ for an $A$-module $M$. A short exact sequence of modules gives a sectionwise short exact sequence of constant presheaves. Exact module-presheaf sheafification therefore makes $L$ exact. The sections functor $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ is exact on all $B$-modules by point-sections exactness. Since $s$ is nonempty, connected, separated and of finite type over $k$, clause (1) of the connected constant-$H^0$ lemma gives $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma B$, $a\mapsto a\cdot1$. The adjunction used in point reconstruction is exactly $L\dashv\Gamma$: its maps send $h:LM\to F$ to $m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m)$ and send $t:M\to\Gamma F$ to $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$. Thus all the exactness and constant-value hypotheses of that reconstruction statement hold. Its natural counit $e_C:Lc\to C$, where $c=\Gamma C$, is an isomorphism, since $C$ is bounded constructible. The fibre definition places $c$ in the bounded finite-cohomology module category. Denote the derived adjunction unit by $u_c:c\to\Gamma Lc$; its triangle identity is $\Gamma(e_C)u_c=1_c$.

source.place: Second sentence: reconstruct the bounded constructible point complex from its module of sections.

proof.text:
Choose a K-flat flat-term module complex $P$ representing $c$, by the K-flat-resolution lemma on the one-object ringed site, and a K-injective resolution $B\to I$ as in the definition of derived internal Hom. Apply the finite case $(R,B)=(A,A_s)$ of the point-derived-Hom-evaluation lemma, whose hypotheses were verified in Step 2. It gives a K-injective module resolution $A\to\Gamma I$ and the natural isomorphism of complexes
$$q_{P,I}:\Gamma\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(LP,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,\Gamma I),\qquad h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x)).$$
Both sides use the same Hom differential $dh=d_Ih-(-1)^{\deg h}hd_P$. Consequently it induces an isomorphism $q_c:\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,A)$. Composing the target change by $\alpha$ of Step 1, precomposition with $e_C$ of Step 2, and $q_c$, gives an isomorphism
$$\beta_C:\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\omega_{s,n})\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,A).$$
Here $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ on the internal-Hom object is the ambient termwise-sections functor of the point-exactness lemma; no assumption that the pro-etale topos itself is the category of sets is used.

source.place: Second sentence: compute point internal Hom over the coefficient ring on K-flat/K-injective models.

proof.text: Identify the map, retaining $\alpha$ as the specified normalization. First, the point-fibre tensor comparison applies to the pair $(R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\omega_{s,n}),C)$: the constant sheaf $B$ is constructible on the single stratum $s$ with finite stalk $A$ and has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, since $B\otimes^L_AM=M$; so the finite-coefficient internal-Hom corollary, applied on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $s$ with $d=0$, puts $R\mathcal Hom_B(C,B)$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$, and $\alpha$ of Step 1 transports this to $R\mathcal Hom_B(C,\omega_{s,n})$. The point-derived-Hom-evaluation lemma says that $q_c$ carries sheaf evaluation to module evaluation under the canonical sections-tensor balancing map. For the convention with factors ordered $P\otimes\operatorname{Hom}$, both maps on $x\in P^i$ and homogeneous $h$ of degree $j$ give $(-1)^{ij}h(1\otimes x)$; symmetry gives the corresponding equality with Hom first as in the statement. Precomposition with $e_C$ evaluates this formula on $\Gamma(e_C)u_c(x)$, which is $x$ by Step 2. Thus after the point-fibre tensor and unit comparisons, evaluation composed with $\beta_C\otimes1_c$ is exactly the fibre of sheaf evaluation followed by $\Gamma\alpha$. Those tensor and unit comparisons are the ones of the point-fibre-derived-tensor lemma: at finite level they are the canonical balancing maps just used. By uniqueness of the tensor-Hom transpose this identifies $\beta_C=\kappa_C$. In particular the actual specified map, rather than merely its source and target objects, is invertible.

source.place: Second sentence: identify the isomorphism by the signed evaluation pairing.

proof.text:
For a morphism $f:C\to C'$, naturality of reconstruction gives $f e_C=e_{C'}L(\Gamma f)$. Precomposition with this equality and naturality of $q$ give
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Gamma f,A)\,\kappa_{C'}=\kappa_C\,\Gamma\bigl(R\mathcal Hom_B(f,\omega_{s,n})\bigr).$$
The equality is in the derived category: $q$ is the natural comparison of derived functors in the cited evaluation lemma, and $e$ is the natural derived counit in reconstruction, so it applies to derived morphisms, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. The normalization $\alpha$ is fixed independently of $C$. This proves the asserted contravariant naturality.

source.place: Second sentence: naturality of the point identification in the complex.
